notes.title: The Stay Positive Update
notes.content: [p]New Meat is now certified Positive on Steam, with ten reviews and counting!  As a way of saying thanks, I've added ten new Curios to the game!  Welcome to The Stay Positive Update![/p][p][/p][p]What's it got?[/p][p][/p][h1]10 New Curios![/h1][p][/p][p]That's right!  Ten all-new Curios are waiting in the Meat Dungeon, and these are some of the wildest yet.  Get a peek at upcoming bosses with the 8-Ball, turn extra keys into energy with the Practice Lock, or use the Bubblegum Wrapper to get extra special reward rooms at the cost of no healing springs.[/p][p][/p][p]A loose theme of these new Curios is one of trade-offs.  Rather than just providing small, passive buffs, most of these new ones ask you to make some kind of trade-off for a much bigger bonus.  My goal is for every Curio you pick up to change the way you play in some manner, and these new Curios really push that "game changer" angle farther than most.[/p][p][/p][h1]And more...?[/h1][p][/p][p]I also added some notable upgrades to a...secret mechanic with which some of you might be familiar.  Unfortunately spoiler tags are being weird, so you'll just have to find it for yourself.[/p][p][/p][p][i]Or maybe it will find you.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]...[/p][p][/p][p]Oh, and I fixed some spelling and collision things.[/p][p][/p][p]Anyway, enjoy the update![/p]

notes.title: The New Meat "It's May" Sale!
notes.content:
Happy end of May, everyone!  The breezes are warming, the flowers are blooming, and the promise of a vibrant summer is upon us!  To celebrate this beautiful changing of the seasons, and for no other reason at all, I'm holding the New Meat "It's May" Sale!

From May 23rd through Memorial Day weekend, all the way to the 30th, New Meat will be a full half-off!  Wow!  That's so much money!  How could you not want to pick up this incredibly beloved game right now?  Already have it?  Buy a copy for a friend!  Share the gifts of May with everyone you care about!

From my family to yours, a safe and happy end of May to all!  Merry Gaming, everyone!

,,,

Why are you looking at me like that?

...

What?

...

[i]What?! [/i] There's no ulterior reason I'm doing this!

...

I-I can't randomly put the game on sale for no reason at all?  Is that what you're saying?  I can't be a nice and generous person?  [i]I can't sew some spontaneous joy on this sunblasted hellscape of a planet Earth?  Is that it?  You think I can't...I can't...[/i]

...

Okay fine, here's what going on.

I've been trying for [i]weeks[/i] to push New Meat over the 10 review line, and I'd really like to get it there in the next month or so for...behind-the-scenes reasons.  I know a lot of people have New Meat wishlisted, so I figured this was a good time for a sale to potentially get a few more eyes on the game.

If you're reading this and picked up the game in the Sale, please consider leaving a review once you've given the game a try.  But don't think I'm just fishing for thumbs-up, here.  Positive or negative, I want to hear what you think.  This isn't just about the review count either (though that is, I want to stress, VERY IMPORTANT).  I also just want to hear your feedback!  The updates to the game thus far have all come out of community responses, so don't hold back and just tell me what you think.

Oh, and I really do want you to have a happy end of May as well.  I wasn't making that up.

notes.title: The Achieve Your Dreams Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the Achieve Your Dreams Update, the first content update for New Meat, based on YOUR feedback (among other things).  There's quite a lot here, so let's dive in!

[h1]DIFFICULTY MODS![/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45458329/707dbf3526a11aca13d50b6d763b24fba1dbcc21.png[/img]

The centerpiece of this update is the all-new Difficulty Mod system!  Under the restaurant, you'll find seven switches that will make the dungeon more difficult in a number of intriguing ways!  Think of these a bit like the "Covenants" from Monster Train, but you get to pick your poison.  Or you can turn them all on for a truly absurd challenge!

Difficulty Mods are accessed via a cheat code entered into the bathroom door panel.  In normal play, you can learn this code by getting the Model Employee ending.  But if you really want to get in there right away...[spoiler]use the code 99999.  Just remember, the code must be entered RIGHT AT THE START of the game, before you kill the first Meathead.[/spoiler]

Right now, the rewards for using Difficulty Mods are fairly minimal, but future updates will put more and more content behind higher and higher difficulties, so you should probably start getting used to them.

[h1]NEW CURIOS![/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45458329/e02981d01946b172d85e38ba259e37c7f96e1a76.png[/img]

Twelve new Curios have been added to the game, and this collection is rather special.  Each one is a sneaky reference to another indie roguelite.  Some references run deeper than others, so be sure to grab them all and see if you can puzzle out what each one is referring to!

And if you want a hint, you might be able to find one somewhere on social media.

[h1]A NEW ENDING?![/h1]

This update adds one new ending to the game, but I’ll leave you to find it on your own.  The only pointers I’ll give you are.

1. It has nothing to do with the Difficulty Mods.
2. It has nothing to do with the new Curios.
3. It’s an ending that probably should have been in the base game.  And, in fact, some of you might have already attempted the thing that triggers it, hoping to get an alternate ending.

And the rest you’ll need to figure out yourselves.  Just be warned, this ending isn’t a happy one.

[h1]AND MORE...?[/h1]

In additional to all that, this update includes some balance and bugfix changes, including a rather important one that fixes how Curses work.  Details below:

-Fixed a bug that caused the Hypergeographic Calculator to not calculate properly when dealing with crystals.

-Fixed a bug that caused the Hypergeographic Calculator to not calculate at all when dealing with Prize Rocks.

-Fixed a bug that would cause Trash Piles to turn invisible but not despawn if you hit the Powerball jackpot.

-Fixed a bug that caused Niko's luck to inversely impact Trash Pile drop rates from how it's supposed to.

-Fixed several related bugs that made Activated Curios behave incorrectly outside the dungeon.

-Being Cursed now has a new animation.  I’m not gonna say it’s better, but it’s less obtrusive.

-Fixed a serious bug that caused Curses to wear off if you lost a Heart in battle.

-Added a new note from Natalie that should help clue people in to the game's core loop

-Stat buffs and debuffs can now only stack up to 2x.  You probably didn't even know stat buffs/debuffs went up to 4x before, but now they don't.



And that's...almost everything, but the rest you can find yourselves.  Thanks to everyone who's supported this game and sent in their feedback.  There's more to come, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Unfortunate News Regarding Achievements
notes.content:
Hi everyone!  Been a bit silent over here for the past couple weeks, because I've been pulling together New Meat's first big update!  This one will have new features, new curios, new lore and even a new ending to see!   But...um...there's one thing it won't have...nor will the game probably ever have it.

[h1]ACHIEVEMENTS (likely) AREN'T COMING TO NEW MEAT![/h1]

Unfortunately, the compatibility issues with RPG Maker MV which prevented achievements from working at launch have proven insurmountable.  What I thought was a simple failed handshake has proven to be a fundamental mismatch in how MV's file structure and the Steam backend are willing to talk to each other.  I've had a commissioned programmer digging through the nw.js documentation for over a month looking for a solution, but they've come up empty.  I'm not saying it's impossible, but it's clear that solving this puzzle could easily take weeks or months of manhours that would be better spent actually improving the game.

I deeply apologize that a promised feature won't be appearing in this game.  I've done everything I can to make it possible, but looking around, larger and more experienced teams than my own have failed in this task before me.  I'm not saying Achievements will never happen in New Meat, but I'm no longer promising it as an upcoming feature.

If you want to refund the game, I perfectly understand.  I know it's a small feature, but a promise is a promise, especially when you're selling someone something.

But I hope you stick around, because the next update is going to be something very special, and with the achievement feature cut, I'm going to redouble my efforts to make this new update worth coming back for.  Cutting bait on this feature will probably be a net positive for the game in the end, and you're just about to get a taste of what I mean.

Coming very soon, get ready for the (now somewhat unfortunately named) ACHIEVE YOUR DREAMS UPDATE!

notes.title: Small Patch: The Antifreeze Update
notes.content:
Hi All!

Achievements are still in the works, but in the meantime, I wanted to push an update to address a problem people have been running into with the game freezing.  This is an issue caused by RPG Maker's incompatibility with high-refresh-rate monitors, but I've located a hotfix that should solve the problem.  Welcome to The Antifreeze Update!

There's a slight chance this hotfix will introduce other unforeseen issues, but my testing didn't reveal anything.  I'll be watching the discussion threads closely.  (One man dev and all that.)

This update also fixes some minor spelling and collision issues that aren't really worth getting into.

notes.title: New Meat is Live!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!  New Meat is now live on Steam!  I'm so happy to finally share this game with the wider world, and I hope you all have just as much fun playing it as I did putting it together.

And even though this is 1.0, development is far from over.  I want to hear your feedback (and about any bugs) and I've got free content planned for the future as well!  I don't have a full roadmap yet, since it's going to rely somewhat on what people want and what elements they respond to, but I can tell you what the next update will be all about.

[strike][h1][u][b]ACHIEVEMENTS![/b][/u][/h1]

Yeah...so...I'll come clean.  You may have noticed Steam Achievements are disabled.  Unfortunately, I discovered a compatibility issue with Steamworks very close to launch that was causing achievements to not work properly.  I have someone hard at work digging into the SDK documentation to figure out what's going on, and while it almost looked like we'd have achievements working for launch, at the eleven-and-a-halfth hour we admitted defeat.

We're confident we can get achievements working and it should only take a little more time, but they're off while we figure things out.

But don't worry!  The update that adds achievements will also include some new free content to play with, just as a make-good, and a preview of what's to come.[/strike]

EDIT: Unfortunately, this will not be a thing.  The compatibility issue I mentioned has proven insurmountable at this time.

Enjoy your first week at work, everyone!
